original_question: A diffeomorphism between two strongly pseudoconvex CR (2n + 1)-manifolds is called quasiconformal if its differential preserves the underlying contact structures and distorts the CR structures boundedly. When Hermitian metrics on the contact bundles are fixed, this distortion can be measured by checking how spheres in the contact space is mapped to ellipsoids. However, this measurement depends on the choices of the Hermitian metrics if n > 1. Fixing a quasiconformal diffeomorphism, can we choose Hermitian metrics so that the distortion is minimal? - Puqi Tang, tang@math.purdue.edu
target_in_paper: An unnumbered problem-list entry by Puqi Tang in arXiv:math/9509202 about higher-dimensional quasiconformal diffeomorphisms of strongly pseudoconvex CR manifolds, specifically whether one can choose Hermitian metrics on the contact bundles so that the resulting quasiconformal distortion is minimized.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the mathematical setting (strongly pseudoconvex CR manifolds of real dimension 2n+1), the relevant class of maps (diffeomorphisms preserving the contact distributions and distorting the CR structures in a bounded way), the geometric meaning of the distortion via how unit spheres in the contact spaces are sent to ellipsoids, and the key higher-dimensional issue that this distortion depends on the chosen Hermitian metrics when n>1. It also correctly asks the natural optimization question suggested by that dependence.
missing_details: The manifolds should be stated as smooth strongly pseudoconvex CR manifolds with contact bundles H_M and H_N and CR structures J_M and J_N.
The map should be fixed as a smooth quasiconformal diffeomorphism f:(M,H_M,J_M)->(N,H_N,J_N) with f_*(H_M)=H_N.

The distortion should be defined explicitly from the differential on the contact bundle: at q in M, it is the ratio of the largest to the smallest norm of f_*X over all h_M-unit vectors X in H_qM, measured using Hermitian metrics h_M and h_N on H_M and H_N.
The optimization target should be made explicit: the natural global quantity is the maximal dilatation K_{h_M,h_N}(f)=ess sup_q K_{h_M,h_N}(f)(q), not just an informal notion of 'minimal distortion'.
The class of metrics over which one minimizes should be specified: all Hermitian metrics on the contact bundles, or equivalently all choices compatible with the given CR structures.
The dimensional restriction n>1 should be stated explicitly as the regime where metric-independence fails; in real dimension 3 the analogous ratio is independent of the chosen Hermitian metrics.
If the geometric ellipsoid language is retained, it should be tied directly to the singular values of f_*|_{H_qM} with respect to the chosen Hermitian metrics.
refined_question: Let f:(M,H_M,J_M)->(N,H_N,J_N) be a smooth quasiconformal diffeomorphism between smooth strongly pseudoconvex CR manifolds of real dimension 2n+1 with n>1, and suppose f_*(H_M)=H_N. For Hermitian metrics h_M on H_M and h_N on H_N, define the pointwise distortion by K_{h_M,h_N}(f)(q)=max{|f_*X|_{h_N}: X in H_qM, |X|_{h_M}=1}/min{|f_*X|_{h_N}: X in H_qM, |X|_{h_M}=1}, and the corresponding maximal dilatation by K_{h_M,h_N}(f)=ess sup_{q in M} K_{h_M,h_N}(f)(q). Since, unlike the 3-dimensional case, this distortion depends on the chosen Hermitian metrics when n>1, does there exist a choice of Hermitian metrics h_M and h_N on the contact bundles that minimizes K_{h_M,h_N}(f) among all such choices?
justification: The arXiv item math/9509202 is a problem list, so the target is an unnumbered entry rather than a numbered conjecture or theorem. Your draft is clearly aimed at Tang's higher-dimensional quasiconformal-CR question. The surrounding paper-faithful context is supplied by Tang's later formal treatment: quasiconformal maps are required to preserve contact structures and their distortion is measured by the ratio of maximal to minimal stretching on the contact bundle; Tang then explicitly notes that the independence of this ratio from the chosen Hermitian metrics is special to real dimension 3 and fails in higher dimensions. That is exactly the hidden premise behind your draft, and it shows that the sharp standalone formulation should ask for a minimizing choice of Hermitian metrics for the resulting maximal dilatation.
